news.title: Jensen Huang reportedly prepared crisis management ahead of personal revelation
news.description: According to Wired, the Nvidia chief reportedly hired a scandal-management firm at least a year before acknowledging an affair with a former Megaspeed executive. Nvidia’s board has launched an independent investigation into the company’s possible ties to China.

news.title: Instagram expands detection of teens lying about their age
news.description: Meta is rolling out worldwide on Instagram an AI system to detect teens who entered a false adult birth date. These accounts are automatically switched to Teen Accounts, with restrictions on contacts, content and time spent.

news.title: Apple wants to turn Siri into a more autonomous assistant
news.description: Apple is working to make Siri an assistant capable of pursuing goals, deciding on next steps, and independently carrying out certain tasks. The change could arrive as early as next year, according to Bloomberg.

news.title: Jensen Huang scandal unlikely to derail the AI market
news.description: Despite Nvidia’s 4.3% drop, the scandal is not expected to trigger a collapse in the artificial intelligence market. Analysts explain why the sector could continue to advance.

news.title: ChatGPT exceeds 81% of traffic among leading AI chatbots
news.description: ChatGPT now accounts for more than 81% of traffic to the six leading AI chatbots, according to a Graphite study. Its growth resumed after a period of stagnation, widening its lead over Claude and Gemini.

news.title: Faith-based investor downplays the importance of Anthropic’s IPO
news.description: A faith-based investor shares his view on Anthropic’s IPO and says the company is not the savior of the universe.

news.title: Anthropic launches Claude Fable 5.2 and formalizes Fermat in 30 hours
news.description: Anthropic introduces Claude Fable 5.2, its most powerful public model, as well as Mythos 5.2 for verified organizations. One thousand Fable 5.2 agents formalized a proof of Fermat’s Last Theorem in Lean in 30 hours.

news.title: OpenAI tests its agents on real-world biology experiments
news.description: With biotech company Ligo, OpenAI is launching BioBasicsBench, a test of 100 tasks based on raw experimental data. The agents must interpret DNA gels, culture plates, microscope images and flow cytometry, among other tasks.

news.title: Google adds two specialized chips to its TPU 8 lineup
news.description: The TPU 8tx encrypts sensitive data while it is being processed, while the TPU 8i Max doubles computing power and memory by combining two chips. Google now has nearly 100 external customers for its TPUs.

news.title: Google’s AI video model cuts prices by 30%
news.description: Google’s Omni 1.2 Flash cuts the cost of AI video generation by 30% and produces clips of up to 15 seconds. It can generate 720p videos for $0.07 per second, with multi-turn editing and improved consistency.

news.title: Disney and Adobe to create AI image models trained on the Disney universe
news.description: Disney is developing its own AI image models based on its characters, settings and styles. The multi-year partnership with Adobe is expected to produce generators for parks, cruises, production and marketing, among other uses.

news.title: OpenAI makes ChatGPT Enterprise available in AWS Marketplace
news.description: AWS customers can now purchase ChatGPT Enterprise through cloud billing and their existing spending commitments.

news.title: OpenAI deploys a kill switch to stop research tasks
news.description: The mechanism blocks a research model’s output within 35 seconds after a person or monitoring system stops the task.

news.title: SpaceX seeks tax relief for its $24 billion energy project
news.description: SpaceX is seeking tax relief for the initial phases of a gas-fired power plant and a supercomputer project valued at about $24 billion at Starbase, Texas.

news.title: Amazon’s Astro home robot attempts a fresh start
news.description: Amazon’s Astro home robot still has fans, but appears destined for abandonment despite the company’s efforts to revive the project.

news.title: Latest figures shed light on AI’s impact on office jobs
news.description: The latest data are being examined to determine whether AI is eliminating office jobs.

news.title: ChatGPT Images 2.6 animates images into GIFs
news.description: OpenAI launched Images 2.6, a ChatGPT update capable of adding subtle motion to any image to create a short GIF. Image generation is also about 50% faster.

news.title: OpenAI merges ChatGPT’s Chat and Work tabs
news.description: OpenAI is merging ChatGPT’s Chat and Work tabs into a single platform, according to TechCrunch. Codex remains separate but shares the same usage quota.

news.title: Owner remains satisfied with his 2018 Tesla Model 3
news.description: An owner says he has a 2018 Model 3 Long Range and is completely satisfied with it despite the additional features of newer models.

news.title: OpenAI reportedly raises $11 billion at a $1.25 trillion valuation
news.description: OpenAI has reportedly secured $11 billion in a funding round that could reach $20 billion, valuing the company at $1.25 trillion. The deal, smaller than expected, comes amid heightened scrutiny of infrastructure spending and AI profitability.

news.title: OpenAI introduces GPT-6 Cyber, a model specialized in cybersecurity
news.description: OpenAI introduced GPT-6 Cyber, a model designed for authorized cybersecurity tasks such as vulnerability research and patch validation. It is currently limited to approved customers in the Daybreak Red program.

news.title: OpenAI acquires Pierre Computer Company to improve Codex
news.description: OpenAI is acquiring Pierre Computer Company to integrate its Git Code.Storage infrastructure into Codex. The technology and its open-source libraries are intended to improve collaboration between human developers and coding agents.

news.title: An AI proves a mathematical conjecture
news.description: AI systems are now producing proofs of open scientific and mathematical problems at a difficult-to-follow pace. Lean certificates provide a validity guarantee, although many proofs still need to be checked by humans.

news.title: Scandal raises questions about Jensen Huang’s future at Nvidia
news.description: Nvidia’s board must investigate whether its CEO was the target of a foreign intelligence operation. The case raises questions about his remaining at the company’s helm and about the future of the AI market.

news.title: Debate intensifies over whether Jensen Huang should remain in his role
news.description: Technology industry figures and investors are debating whether Jensen Huang can remain CEO of Nvidia after the scandal involving him. Donald Trump supports him, while some investors believe his departure is likely.

news.title: Who could replace Jensen Huang at Nvidia?
news.description: Replacing Jensen Huang would be particularly complex because he runs Nvidia day to day and embodies both the company and the AI industry. Geoff Weiss examines the candidates who could succeed him.

news.title: Wall Street strategists bet on an AI rebound again
news.description: After the sell-off that hit the AI market following the midterm elections, investors are buying the dip. Strategists now expect gains by the end of the year.

news.title: Morgan Stanley proposes a three-part strategy for investing in AI
news.description: Morgan Stanley considers the market’s reaction to the Democratic wave in the midterm elections excessive. The bank recommends betting on hyperscalers, data-center providers and companies adopting AI.

news.title: Goldman Sachs’ new partners describe how they celebrated their promotions
news.description: Goldman Sachs promoted 109 people to its partnership. Six new partners describe how they learned the news and celebrated their promotions.

news.title: TikTok Shop increases the influence of its Chinese executives
news.description: A leaked organizational chart reveals that China-based executives have increased their power over TikTok Shop. ByteDance sold much of its stake in the U.S. version while retaining tight control of Shop.

news.title: California billionaires avoid a new tax
news.description: California voters rejected Proposition 40, which would have imposed a one-time 5% tax on fortunes exceeding $1 billion. Silicon Valley leaders largely funded the opposition campaign.

news.title: An $8 surcharge reveals the scale of hidden fees in the U.S.
news.description: A journalist thought she would pay $20 for a haircut before discovering an $8 surcharge. The experience led her to investigate the hidden-fee epidemic, estimated at $90 billion.

news.title: Andrew Huberman joins the Hims&Hers board of directors
news.description: Stanford neuroscientist and podcaster Andrew Huberman is joining the Hims&Hers board of directors. He will advise the company directly on scientific issues and marketing without changing the topics of his podcast.

news.title: Disney+ prepares creator content and a free tier
news.description: Disney’s technology executives presented Disney+’s priorities for the coming year. They include expanding into creator content and launching a free offering.

news.title: Skydance executives address employees after strong results
news.description: Skydance’s CEOs spoke to employees after the company beat forecasts in its first earnings report.

news.title: Four tech CEOs explain how they handled romantic scandals
news.description: The article examines how four technology executives handled scandals related to their personal relationships.

news.title: Former Cohere employees launch a law firm after leaving
news.description: Employees left Cohere to pursue careers in law. They say their new firm can avoid the fate experienced by Weil.

news.title: Paramount+ and HBO Max to prepare a bundle
news.description: A bundle combining Paramount+ and HBO Max is in the works. Skydance has outlined the timeline for bringing its streaming services together.

news.title: James Gunn and Peter Safran leave DC Studios
news.description: James Gunn and Peter Safran will step down from their roles at DC Studios.

news.title: Apple harvest expected to be very poor for U.S. orchards
news.description: Local apple orchards are experiencing an especially difficult year.

news.title: Legal startup generates $150 million without targeting major firms
news.description: A legal startup says it generates $150 million in revenue without seeking to compete directly with major law firms.

news.title: Meituan releases LongCat-2.5, a very low-cost open-source coding model
news.description: Meituan is releasing the weights of LongCat-2.5 under the MIT license, a multimodal model capable of analyzing screenshots and videos before coding in multiple steps. Its API access is priced at $0.30 per million input tokens, compared with $5 for Claude Opus 5.

news.title: Bytedance unveils Seedream 5.5 for editing an image up to 100 times
news.description: Seedream 5.5 is designed to support up to 100 successive edits while preserving unchanged areas and colors. The model also natively generates RGBA images and is gradually rolling out across several Bytedance services.

news.title: Meta launches Muse Ember, nearly as capable as its larger model
news.description: Meta is launching Muse Ember, a small model designed for agents’ repetitive tasks, such as tool calling, routing and data extraction. It achieves nearly the same score as Muse Spark 1.3 at 17 times lower cost per task.

news.title: HOPE halves a large model without retraining
news.description: Amazon researchers propose HOPE, a method that removes the least useful experts while accounting for their interactions. It removes 50% of the experts and notably improves agentic coding performance compared with the best competing method.

news.title: Law firms split between time savings and resistance to agents
news.description: Legal industry leaders describe the gains enabled by agents, including bringing outsourced tasks back in-house. Many lawyers, however, remain limited to document summaries out of fatigue or fear of losing billable time.

news.title: Paramount chief sees AI as a major transformation for cinema
news.description: David Ellison calls AI “the greatest creative lever in modern history” and compares it with the arrival of computer-generated imagery in the 1990s. No concrete project has been announced, however.

news.title: Researchers propose “cognitive symbiotes” rather than autonomous agents
news.description: A paper proposes persistent AI companions that remember context, spot forgotten details, and intervene at the right moment. The approach aims to strengthen human thinking, but remains conceptual and raises risks involving dependence, privacy, and equity.

news.title: Muir improves model efficiency on long texts
news.description: Muir is a linear-attention architecture that focuses its resources on the most important information in internal memory. On small models, it retrieves information from long documents more effectively and speeds up training by 2.7 times at 32K context.

news.title: DeepX announces a chip capable of running 100 billion parameters under 5 watts
news.description: Korean manufacturer DeepX claims it can run models with up to 100 billion parameters using less than 5 watts. The second-generation chip is ready for manufacturing, but the announced gains remain manufacturer projections.

news.title: Coalition opposes Google data center near London
news.description: In Thurrock, the Buglife association, the Foxglove NGO, and a motorcycle club delivered a petition with nearly 55,000 signatures to Google. They denounce the project’s effects on a rare plant and bumblebee, pollution, and the disappearance of a former motorcycle circuit.

news.title: Claude Code exposed passwords in GitHub repositories
news.description: The “Yes, and don't ask again” option can record commands containing secrets in the .claude/settings.local.json file. Apiiro found 1,379 distinct secrets in public copies of this file.

news.title: Tencent wants to remove dangerous knowledge from training data
news.description: Tencent’s chief AI scientist believes AI will soon be able to design biological weapons, but says closing models is not a solution. For its future open model Hy4, Tencent wants to remove dangerous knowledge directly from the training data.

news.title: U.S. companies without employees are growing with AI
news.description: In sectors exposed to AI, new businesses with no plans to hire increased by 26.8% between early 2024 and early 2026. New businesses planning to hire fell by 6.4%, but a causal link to AI has not yet been established.

news.title: Claude uncovers more than 100 vulnerabilities in UK government projects
news.description: Using Claude Opus and Sonnet, a researcher found vulnerabilities in about two-thirds of 349 public projects belonging to 33 UK organizations. One vulnerability provided read and write access to SharePoint and OneDrive spaces containing HR records.

news.title: Trump downplays AI risks on 60 Minutes
news.description: Donald Trump says the risk posed by AI is “far less real” than industry leaders claim and says it is being controlled by the Department of Justice. He also recounts an unverifiable anecdote about an AI company executive threatened with prison.

news.title: Nothing will launch its first AI device in December
news.description: Nothing will launch its first AI-native productivity device in December, without a new screen. Carl Pei mentions previously unseen contextual features, with details to be revealed soon.

news.title: Aina’s AI ring turns the thumb into an approval button
news.description: Aina’s ring, sold for 399 dollars, offers contextual actions that can be approved with a thumb movement, such as booking a ride, managing meetings, or answering calls. IT professionals should especially verify compatibility, permissions, and audit trails.

news.title: Nvidia strengthens AI chip tracking in Southeast Asia
news.description: Nvidia now requires its Southeast Asian cloud partners to enroll in Fleet Intelligence to improve GPU tracking, amid allegations of chip smuggling to China. The measure could affect partner status, GPU availability, and compliance with export rules.

news.title: Cursor can create and deploy web applications from prompts
news.description: Cursor’s Build Live Apps feature generates, secures, and deploys complete applications with a database, authentication, and hosting. It aims to reduce the setup time for internal tools, but its security and pricing limitations should be examined.

news.title: Anthropic’s AI progress has nearly doubled
news.description: Anthropic’s benchmark scores improved by 1.9 times, but hidden elements warn that speed does not necessarily mean better results. IT buyers should test models on real-world tasks, evaluating completion, review time, cost, and reliability in particular.

news.title: AI is becoming widespread as threats and pressures increase
news.description: AI is being deployed everywhere and creating new security and infrastructure problems. Generative advances, attacks, and cost pressures are reshaping business priorities.

news.title: Five Canva alternatives for businesses in 2027
news.description: Adobe Express, Visme, VistaCreate, Figma, and Piktochart each address specific professional needs, from branding to data visualization. The article recommends testing these solutions for two weeks before switching tools.

news.title: AI data center boom sparks political backlash in the United States
news.description: Voters have opposed the growth of AI-focused data centers, and new restrictions could slow construction, raise costs, and alter how capacity is distributed. The regions, regulations, and business risks involved remain areas to monitor.

news.title: Fireworks AI confirms billing and model data leak
news.description: Attackers accessed customer billing data, excluding card numbers, as well as model weights and incomplete datasets for some customers. Fireworks links the incident to a group that resells access to stolen AI accounts.

news.title: Cisco integrates Anthropic’s Claude Mythos into its AI defense offering
news.description: Cisco plans to add Claude Mythos to AI Defense so that some companies can run adaptive red-team tests on their own AI applications.

news.title: Liquid Energy unveils NanoDC, a prefabricated solar AI data center
news.description: The Y Combinator startup claims that NanoDC, a factory-built solar data center for AI, can be deployed in four weeks. These figures are stated by the company.

news.title: Adobe study says AI is accelerating growth for many creators
news.description: According to Adobe’s survey, 78% of creative AI users believe these tools have accelerated the growth of their business or audience. The study also says that 68% accept results that do not match their vision at least sometimes.

news.title: Why AI pilots still struggle to reach enterprise scale
news.description: The article examines why successful AI pilot projects still struggle to be deployed at scale across enterprises.

news.title: The Value Stack helps prioritize customer benefits
news.description: Customers do not place equal importance on every benefit: some determine their choice, others reinforce it, while “table stakes” are simply expected. Strategyzer proposes the Value Stack to organize these benefits into three categories and build a more differentiated value proposition.

news.title: Huawei builds the first fully Chinese-made PC
news.description: Huawei says it designed the Qingyun HM650 using components sourced entirely from China, along with its HarmonyOS Enterprise operating system and Kirin X90 chip. A Chinese government agency has reportedly ordered 600 units.

news.title: Coinbase receives a full federal banking charter in the United States
news.description: Coinbase has received a full national trust company charter from the U.S. federal banking regulator.

news.title: AMD acknowledges driver bug that wears out SSDs by writing continuously
news.description: AMD acknowledged that a graphics driver bug continuously wrote data, potentially accelerating SSD wear.

news.title: Nvidia GR00T 2 teaches robots precise movements through human videos
news.description: Nvidia’s GR00T 2 model enables robots to learn delicate skills from videos showing humans.

news.title: Apple responds to allegations of unauthorized subscriptions
news.description: Apple employees are accused of signing customers up for subscriptions without their consent. The company has responded to the allegations.

news.title: Linus Torvalds believes the influx of AI-generated patches has peaked
news.description: Linus Torvalds sees signs that the wave of patches generated with AI prompts has reached its peak.

news.title: AI causes a widespread collapse of signals
news.description: An article claims that AI is simultaneously causing signals to collapse across many fields.

news.title: Fine-tuning can remove propaganda from some Chinese AI models
news.description: A study indicates that state propaganda present in some Chinese AI models is only a “thin layer” that can be removed through fine-tuning.

news.title: Two Chinese companies authorized to buy restricted Nvidia chips cannot be found
news.description: Two Chinese companies authorized to purchase restricted Nvidia AI chips have empty offices and unknown addresses.

news.title: Waymo robotaxis continued illegally passing school buses
news.description: According to U.S. federal authorities, Waymo robotaxis continued illegally passing school buses after a software fix.

news.title: Claude Skills replace copied-and-pasted prompts with slash commands
news.description: Skills save detailed instructions to a Claude account so they can be reused in every new conversation. The /skill-creator command can generate custom Skills based on tone, format and audience preferences.

news.title: Cisco relies on partners to innovate and deploy AI
news.description: At Cisco Partner Summit 2026, Pascal Bornet said partners account for about 90% of Cisco’s bookings and have far greater sales and technical capabilities than the company. Cisco wants to become the “plumber” consulted from the design stage of projects, as value shifts toward technology implementation, operation and continuous improvement.

news.title: Claude launches a personal finance hub
news.description: Anthropic introduced Personal Finance in Claude, a beta feature that lets users connect bank accounts and cards to ask natural-language questions about their spending. Access is read-only and currently limited to Pro, Max and Ultra subscribers in the United States.

news.title: Netflix tests a mood-based AI Discover tab
news.description: Netflix unveiled AI Discover, a tab in its TV app that recommends programs based on AI-generated mood themes such as “Scare Me” and “Quick Watches.” The rollout is beginning with English-speaking members in the United States.

news.title: Anthropic publishes a tutorial for building apps with Claude Artifacts
news.description: Anthropic published a detailed tutorial on using Claude Artifacts to visualize data and build AI applications without writing code.

news.title: Accelerator and autonomous driving: can you intervene safely?
news.description: A driver asks whether it is possible to press the accelerator at certain moments when autonomous driving occasionally slows the car down.

news.title: Driver shares experience without access to fast charging
news.description: A Tesla owner describes spending a day without access to DC fast charging and outlines the positive and negative aspects.

news.title: Inconsistencies observed in Full Self-Driving mode
news.description: A discussion focuses on inconsistencies in Full Self-Driving mode, particularly its speed profiles, which are not considered 100% reliable but appear to be improving with updates.

news.title: Disable “Hey Grok” to avoid surveillance
news.description: A post recommends disabling the “Hey Grok” feature to avoid being monitored by Grok.

news.title: Drivers look for ways to change FSD routes
news.description: Users share several methods for getting a route different from the one selected by the navigation system, including checking settings or adding an intermediate stop.

news.title: Scam uses Lars Moravy’s name to sell Teslas
news.description: A user reports a fraudulent email titled “Exclusive Tesla Inventory Opportunity – Special Purchase Pricing,” sent from a Gmail address claiming to belong to Lars Moravy.

news.title: How many physical key cards should come with a Tesla?
news.description: A user asks how many physical keys are provided with a Tesla.

news.title: A hole in a 2018 Model 3’s trunk increases noise
news.description: The owner of a 2018 Model 3 Long Range says they discovered a hole between the rear speakers that was causing significant noise from the trunk.

news.title: Thinking Machines launches its second-generation AI model
news.description: Inkling 2 Small is described as capable in coding, research and long-running office tasks, with particular strength in vision. The model is expected to become the top open-weight model on the DesignArena leaderboard and is already available on Tinker.

news.title: Brian Armstrong shares his personal agent system for working continuously
news.description: Coinbase CEO Brian Armstrong published a personal agent system that would allow him to work on projects 24 hours a day. His post surpassed 11,000 bookmarks and shares.

news.title: The Weather Channel launches a retro weather site with smooth jazz
news.description: The Weather Channel launched a minimalist site displaying local weather with an iconic smooth-jazz soundtrack. The project became less expensive to build thanks to advances in AI software development.

news.title: Peter Thiel-backed startup uses AI to improve the taste of fish
news.description: While most AI startups focus on productivity, a company backed by Peter Thiel is seeking to use AI to make fish taste better.

news.title: Microsoft expands usage restrictions for Copilot Chat in businesses
news.description: Microsoft is expanding usage limits for Microsoft 365 customers without a separate Copilot license. The thresholds remain unknown, and administrators cannot view or modify them.

news.title: Defense in depth must adapt to machine speed
news.description: AI tools are making vulnerability exploitation much cheaper and faster, limiting the effectiveness of late human-led patching. The article recommends reducing exposure, segmenting networks, using virtual patches and prioritizing memory-safe code.

news.title: Companies need to rethink how they buy technology
news.description: Traditional IT procurement often prioritizes specifications and discounts over business outcomes. The article recommends small experiments, outcome-based evaluation and contracts suited to rapidly changing technologies.

news.title: Anthropic strengthens Claude Enterprise security controls
news.description: Anthropic announced new security features for Claude Enterprise, including a security center, inference hooks for preventing data leaks and centralized management. Additional access controls include remote sign-out and support for EDR sensors.

news.title: Snowflake launches public preview of CoCo for Excel and Google Sheets
news.description: Snowflake announced the public preview of CoCo for Excel and Google Sheets, a coding agent that lets users interact with data in natural language. The tool preserves enterprise governance through access controls, semantic views and virtual warehouses.

news.title: Google invests $17 billion in a data center campus
news.description: Google announced a $17 billion investment in its first data center in Wyoming, on a campus previously developed by Crusoe. The project will use natural-gas fuel cells, carbon capture and air cooling.

news.title: Wi-Fi 8 will prioritize reliability and roaming over speed
news.description: The upcoming Wi-Fi 8 standard aims to improve predictability, reliability and roaming in dense environments rather than increase maximum speed. It will introduce multi-access-point coordination and a unified mobility domain.

news.title: NTT Data signs agreement for 900 MW of fuel cells
news.description: NTT Data signed an agreement with Bloom Energy to deploy up to 900 MW of fuel-cell capacity at its data centers worldwide. The first deliveries are expected in 2027.

news.title: Playmobil owner enters the data center business in Germany
news.description: The company behind Playmobil toys plans to transform a former German industrial site into a data center campus, with initial demand potentially reaching 100 MW. The project would target hyperscalers, startups and other customers.

news.title: Atlassian reports strong fiscal 2027 first-quarter results
news.description: In its shareholder letter, Atlassian reported strong results for the first quarter of fiscal 2027. The company highlighted momentum behind its System of Work, powered by Teamwork Graph, Rovo agents and the Agentic Multiplayer Protocol.

news.title: Employees may be more candid with AI than with their managers
news.description: New research suggests employees may sometimes feel more comfortable challenging an AI than their human managers. This trend raises questions about leadership, psychological safety, and problem reporting.

news.title: Companies remain responsible for their AI agents’ mistakes
news.description: Four UK regulators have warned that organizations remain responsible for the autonomous AI agents they deploy.

news.title: Python temporarily abandons its experimental native JIT compiler
news.description: Python is putting its experimental native just-in-time compiler on hold for now due to maintenance issues. The language is nevertheless continuing to evolve its ecosystem and features.

news.title: Large language models are poor at designing AI systems
news.description: Large language models are not good at designing software that itself uses LLMs. Their effectiveness varies widely by task, but predicting their strengths and weaknesses could provide significant value.

news.title: Programming with AI may be more tiring
news.description: Programming is becoming more tiring with AI because it takes over repetitive and obvious tasks. Developers then focus more on tasks that require judgment and thought.

news.title: AI is causing a widespread collapse in trust signals
news.description: AI is making it increasingly difficult to distinguish quality work, poor work, and fake content. It weakens the signals people use to make decisions and reduces the incentive to produce quality work.

news.title: Jevons’ paradox could also displace software jobs
news.description: The amount of software created is expected to grow far faster than the number of people paid to produce it. AI will make many previously undeveloped software projects possible, while demand could remain unlimited.

news.title: How long life can remain in a state of suspended animation
news.description: The length of time an organism can remain inert while staying viable when conditions improve could have major implications for space exploration.

news.title: The value of software intellectual property is collapsing
news.description: Intellectual property is worth approximately what it costs to rebuild, and that cost is now very low.

news.title: A method for combating AI-related cognitive fatigue
news.description: Conventional AI workflows have sequencing and context problems. The article proposes organizing work as a priority queue to overcome them.

news.title: Why having multiple designers on a team can be problematic
news.description: The article argues that having more than one designer on a team creates difficulties.
